question: Do secants of the original marked generic basis produce shared quadratic classes or rational points preferentially on the retained high-gain fibres?
selection: Every unordered pair of marked generic basis points, with relative sign +1 and -1. No exceptional points, labels, scores or ranks in the computation input.
construction: On the original short model F, take the secant L=s*x+h and its x-axis intercept x0=-h/s. Test C=F(x0) for being a rational square; group nonzero C by exact equality in Q*/Q*2.
gate: A shared nonsquare class is only a candidate common quadratic twist, not proven independent directions. A square C supplies a rational point, not a new quotient direction until independence modulo the original generic subgroup is certified. Degenerate secants are separately recorded.
boundary: Retrospective generic-only solubility and class-sharing diagnostic on fixed curves. Does not modify the parent family or any live search, and establishes no absence result outside this finite secant dictionary.
